select.notes: Slot 1 led via the mandate escape hatch (Bloomberg + Economist mandate_count >= 2 on the Iran cluster). Slot 3 was originally drafted as the DOJ/Carroll probe but swapped to the bipartisan ex-judges petition on the Trump IRS settlement because the only reliably fetchable body source on Carroll was CBS (Reuters/BBC/Hill/Guardian/Deutsche Welle all egress-blocked or PerimeterX-walled), failing the two-body-source hard minimum.

research.notes: Egress proxy blocks remain heavy across Reuters, BBC, The Hill, FT, NPR, Politico, AP News (direct), Guardian (direct), DW, Ars Technica, Wired, Axios — all routed via Google News (GN) RSS yesterday for the same reason. Google News landing pages do not expose the destination URL to curl, so GN-routed bodies could not be retrieved today. Body sources came from CNBC, PBS, CBS, NBC, Al Jazeera, and Fox News — direct curl with a browser UA worked for all six.

revise_notes.slot_3: Luttig descriptor included 'Fourth Circuit,' not in dossier — softened to 'former appellate Judge … a well-known conservative jurist who has been critical of Trump' (CBS phrasing).
revise_notes.slot_4: D4vd reference cited 'a Los Angeles homicide investigation' — Los Angeles not in any dossier source; rewrote to drop the jurisdiction claim.
revise_notes.slot_5: Freshness pivot misattributed 'seven cases' to JSJ's Saturday edition (Saturday's headline said five). Rewritten to contrast Saturday's reported five with today's seven.
